say: Welcome. Today is one story in two parts: Copilot in Outlook, then Copilot in Teams.
You're a service coordination officer. You'll triage a mailbox, reply to a resident, summarise a thread and plan a meeting. Then we'll see the same story in Teams.
Everything is fictional, and nothing gets sent.
welcome.ask: What is the first thing you do with a busy inbox today?
welcome.watch: Say the do-not-send rule out loud now. The people who miss it are the ones who press Send later.

say: These four cards are what must be true before Activity 1. We'll make them true in the next few steps.
One rule first: don't use your own or real work email. The practice emails give everyone the same context.
needs.ask: Can you switch between Outlook and this page without losing your place?
needs.watch: Learners sometimes prompt against their real inbox. Remind them the prompts are limited to the Copilot Learning emails.

say: Download the ZIP. It holds eight practice emails: four single messages and four that form one conversation.
Every subject starts with the Copilot Learning tag. That makes them easy to find now, and easy to delete later.
get.ask: Where did your browser save the file?
get.watch: Some learners open the ZIP and drag out one file. Ask for the whole ZIP, then unzip it in the next step.

say: Right-click the ZIP, choose Extract All, then click Extract. A folder opens with eight email files.
Remember where it is. You'll point Outlook at this folder, not at the ZIP.
unzip.ask: Can you see eight files in the folder?
unzip.watch: Outlook can't import from the ZIP itself. The folder has to be extracted first.

say: Open new Outlook for Windows. Choose File, then Open and export.
These import screens are for new Outlook. If your screen looks different, tell me now.
filemenu.watch: If a learner's menus don't match, check which version of Outlook they have before anything else.

say: In Settings, choose Import. Then click Start import under Email Files, dot eml.
Not the Outlook Data File option. That one is for a different kind of file.
importeml.ask: Which of the two import options are you choosing?
importeml.watch: Learners click Get started by mistake. That is the Outlook Data File option, not Email Files.

say: Click Choose and pick the extracted folder. Outlook asks you to confirm the upload of eight files.
Pick the folder, not the ZIP.
upload.ask: How many files does Outlook say it will upload?
upload.watch: Eight is right. A different number usually means the wrong folder.

say: Under Choose destination, create a new folder and name it LEARN-COPILOT. Then click Import.
If the folder is already there from an earlier class, select it instead of creating it again.
destination.ask: What did you name the folder?
destination.watch: A different folder name makes the next search harder. Keep LEARN-COPILOT exactly.

say: Open LEARN-COPILOT and search for the tag. You should find eight emails.
The four upgrade emails can show as one conversation, or you can find them by their shared subject.
check.ask: How many emails and conversations can you see?
check.watch: If something is missing, use the three tips on the right before importing again. Importing twice can give duplicates.

say: That is the set-up done. Eight practice emails are now in Outlook.
Next is Activity 1, triage. You'll stay in the mailbox and ask Copilot.
cp1.ask: Can everyone see the eight emails?
cp1.watch: Don't move on until everyone has them. A missing email breaks Activity 3.

say: Don't open any email. Stay in Outlook and open Copilot.
Copy Prompt 1, paste it and run it. The prompt limits Copilot to the training emails.
Come back when the priority list appears, and compare it with the subjects.
a1.ask: What did Copilot put first, and why?
a1.watch: Learners open an email first. Prompt 1 works across the mailbox, so keep them in the inbox.

say: Tick what you can see in your own answer. Nothing is scored.
Look for reasons, not only a list of subjects. Look for anything marked as unclear rather than guessed.
a1c.ask: Which email did Copilot place first, and what information did it use to justify that priority?
a1c.watch: Answers will differ. Compare the reasons, not the lists.

say: Open Emily Carter's email first. That narrows the context.
Select Reply, then Draft with Copilot, and run Prompt 2.
Read the draft against her message. Don't send it.
a2.ask: What did you check first in the draft?
a2.watch: The risk is an invented promise: a repair date, a reference number or a team name. Nobody sends anything.

say: Check the draft against the original message, one tick at a time.
A good reply thanks her, confirms what she reported and says it has been referred. It gives no date, decision or outcome.
a2c.ask: Did Copilot say anything Emily didn't?
a2c.watch: Make sure the draft is closed, not sent.

say: Two activities done. You've triaged the mailbox and drafted a careful reply.
Next is the upgrade thread.
cp2.ask: Which result did you trust least, and why?
cp2.watch: Use this pause to catch anyone who is behind.

say: Open the upgrade thread. It should include four people: Sarah, Liam, Chloe and Rebecca.
Select Summary by Copilot, read it, then run Prompt 3 as the follow-up.
The four headings separate what is confirmed from what isn't.
a3.ask: Which heading has the most items in your summary?
a3.watch: Here we say Summary by Copilot. Microsoft Learn says Summarize by Copilot. If a learner's button reads differently, it's the same feature.

say: Look for each category in your answer.
Confirmed is the scope and the people. Not yet confirmed is the dates, approval and night work. Then come the decisions needed and the actions.
a3c.ask: Where did Copilot leave an owner or a date unassigned?
a3c.watch: A date presented as final is a warning sign. The thread says dates aren't final until approval.

say: Keep the same thread open. Choose Schedule with Copilot, then Draft with Copilot in the invitation.
Run Prompt 4 for a 30-minute agenda. Don't send the invitation.
a4.ask: What decision does your agenda put first?
a4.watch: Learners open a different email. The agenda has to come from the upgrade thread. Close the draft without sending.

say: Check the agenda: an objective, the roles, and a time and outcome for every item.
The last five minutes confirm actions, owners and dates. Provisional dates must not appear as approved.
a4c.ask: Does your last item confirm actions, owners and dates?
a4c.watch: Again, no sending. Close the meeting draft.

say: That is Part 1: four moves from correspondence to coordinated action.
Triage, acknowledge, summarise and create the agenda. Each time, you checked the result before using it.
The meeting is prepared, so Teams picks up the story.
olrecap.ask: Which of the four would save you the most time?
olrecap.watch: Keep this short. The next part is led from the front.

say: Part 2 starts from the agenda you just built. We don't repeat triage.
The meeting is Wattle Road and Riverside Upgrade Coordination, with five roles.
From here I lead and you watch. I control the pace.
thand.ask: Which of these five roles would you want in the room?
thand.watch: Don't start a new meeting. We use this live session for Demos 1 and 2.

say: I'll show how the meeting is scheduled and where Facilitator is added.
Open the meeting, show Meeting options, then Copilot and other AI, and add Facilitator.
No new meeting starts. Everyone stays in this session.
tsetup.ask: Why might a team choose one meeting option over another?
tsetup.watch: Check the exact menus in your own environment first, because they change.

say: Copilot is private. It helps one person understand the discussion and answers their questions.
Facilitator is shared. It helps the group with the agenda, time, notes and tasks.
The meeting option has to fit the purpose and your organisation's rules. Transcripts and recaps may be records.
tdiff.ask: Which would you use to catch up quietly, and which to keep a group on track?
tdiff.watch: Don't give legal advice. Point people to their own organisation's guidance.

say: First demo, in this live session. I open Copilot in the meeting and run the recap prompt.
It works from what has actually been discussed here, so the recap is only as good as our conversation.
d1.ask: What would you expect the recap to leave out?
d1.watch: Run it in this meeting, not a new one. Read the output before presenting it as reliable.

say: Check it together. Outlook and Teams content should be separate, the cautions visible, and the recap should match what we really covered.
d1c.ask: Does the recap match what we actually discussed?
d1c.watch: If it misses something, say so. That is the lesson.

say: Same Copilot pane, same meeting. Don't switch to the channel yet.
The prompt asks for the action items, with an owner and due date only if stated. Anything missing goes under Needs confirmation.
d2.ask: Which action here has no owner or date?
d2.watch: Copilot must not assign missing owners. If it does, point it out.

say: Each action should be distinct, with owners and dates only when stated.
Incomplete items belong under Needs confirmation. A good list shows what is missing.
d2c.ask: What is still missing from the list?

say: Now the channel. Open the prepared channel and use Copilot there.
The prompt names the time period: the past seven days. It should use only this channel.
Set the channel up beforehand with the messages in the instructor file.
d3.ask: Which thread do you think should come first?
d3.watch: Post the messages on the day, so the seven-day window isn't empty. Use only this channel.

say: Check that the result stays inside the selected channel.
Urgent decisions and blockers should come before routine updates, and you should be able to check the supporting messages.
d3c.ask: Which message supports the first item?
d3c.watch: If it pulls in anything from outside the channel, stop and explain why context matters.

say: Now your turn, if we have time. Choose one prompt: today or this week.
Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in Work mode, check the Work IQ button is on, and paste just one.
try.ask: Today or this week: which will you try?
try.watch: Not both. If time is short, tell learners to take the prompts away as practice.

say: Check the work items before you act on any answer.
Deadlines should stay with the right item, and missing details should be flagged, not invented.
Your results will differ from your neighbour's, because you each have different work content.
tryc.ask: What did Copilot flag as unclear?
tryc.watch: Don't compare screens. People's work content is private.

say: This is the big idea. Where you ask decides what Copilot works from.
In a meeting, it uses the discussion. In a channel, that channel. In Copilot Chat in Work mode, your own work content.
So tell Copilot the context and the time period. Then verify the result before you act.
tcontext.ask: Which context would you use after missing a meeting?
tcontext.watch: Avoid saying Copilot knows everything. It works from the context you give it.

say: Outlook created the agenda. Teams helped move the work forward.
We scheduled the meeting and added Facilitator, recapped the discussion, extracted actions and prioritised a channel.
The quality of the answer depends on the context. Review before acting.
trecap.ask: What will you do differently the next time you write a prompt?
trecap.watch: Keep it brief, then move to what you learned.

say: Five skills: triage the inbox, reply carefully, summarise a thread, build an agenda, and use Copilot in Teams.
Three habits: review before acting, don't send in training, and name the context.
Pick one prompt you'll reuse this week.
learned.ask: Which prompt will you reuse this week?
learned.watch: Close on the habits, not the features.
